newsitem.title: UK: UK's FTSE 100 pares losses, ends slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: UK's FTSE 100 pares losses, ends slightly lower.

text.p: The UK's FTSE 100 index suffered its first setback in the last five sessions on Wednesday as weaker European bourses and concerns about rising yields kept buyers sidelined, dealers said.
The blue chip index slipped 4.1 points to close at 4,677.5, as decliners narrowly outpaced advancers 48 to 45.
UK blue chips trimmed their losses late in the session as the as the Dow, down some 30 points at one stage, swung into positive territory and was up about four points when London markets closed.
U.S. bonds rallied, while bunds and gilts, which had been down sharply for most of the session, also recovered.
But with investors' attention fixed on slumping French shares, it was difficult for the FTSE to make further progress, dealers said.
The CAC 40 was down by as much as 4.4 percent amid worries that the opposition Socialists may be well placed to win a majority of parliamentary seats in Sunday's election.

Dealers noted fears that a coalition of Socialist and Communists, which won the first-round ballot last Sunday, could scrap an austerity drive to qualify for Europe's monetary union if they win this weekend's vote.
Caution was also evident ahead of a statement from the Bundesbank, due at 1700 GMT on Wednesday, regarding the revaluation of German gold reserves.
"This international backdrop is not terribly helpful," said UK equity strategist David McBain of NatWest. "And bond yields are providing some cause for caution."
However, volume was light, which was viewed as an encouraging sign. At 1544 GMT, only 610.2. million shares were registered.
"We're not seeing the kind of heavy selling you might expect," said one dealer.

Added NatWest's McBain, "There are still some outstanding domestic issues ... Institutions are cash-rich and are not desperate to cash in their bets just yet. People are willing to hold fire until they see the contents of the budget and get clarification on corporate tax policies."
The government is expected to release its budget sometime in June or early July.
Among individual top-line UK stocks, shares in Guinness Plc and Grand Metropolitan Plc stumbled after news that LVMH intended to sell all Guinness' interest in their joint ventures.

The move -- which would give LVMH the right to continue marketing and distributing Guinness brands in key markets including China, the U.S. and Japan for at least 10 years -- could delay the proposed 23 billion stg merger between the two companies.
Guinness slid 15-1/2p to 580-1/2, while Grand Met fell 15p to 581-1/2.
Shares in Cable and Wireless Plc jumped 8-1/2p to 494-1/2 after a strong overnight performance from its biggest asset -- Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd.
Hong Kong Telecom shares rose to new year highs amid a buying spree sparked by renewed talk that C&W was poised to sell down its near-60 percent stake to mainland Chinese investors.
Merger talks between America's AT & T Corp and SBC Communications Inc also helped the stock, making one of C&W's potential alliance partners more attractive, analysts said.

Among second-liners, Thorn Plc added 5-1/2p to 155-1/2, after posting full-year pre-tax profits of 171 million stg. The rentals group, which split from EMI Plc last year, also said it intended to return 87 million stg to shareholders.
Shares in Allders Plc climbed 10-1/2 to 214-1/2p, after the UK retailer reported a doubling of first half pre-tax profits and said its second half had started well, dealers said.
Pre-tax profit rose 16.0 million stg from 8.0 million, boosted by buoyant trading.
Elsewhere, shares in small UK water companies raced ahead as bid hopes emerged following the agreed offer from Anglian Water Plc for Hartlepool Water Plc.
-- Debra Sherman, London Newsroom +44 171 542 5106
